key_insight: LW2S learns when a workflow component can be safely skipped by estimating the counterfactual utility of omitting it, rather than assuming every step is always needed.
engineering_relevance: This enables multi-agent LLM systems to cut token cost and latency while preserving accuracy, making staged execution more practical for math reasoning and other structured tasks.
method: Treat component omission as counterfactual credit assignment using full runs plus controlled skip interventions.
Train action-specific safety models to predict when skipping a step is safe.
Use held-out calibration and domain-native guards, with fallback to continue execution if an early skip is rejected.
evidence_signal: The paper reports evaluations on mathematical reasoning, multiple-choice QA, and code generation across two instruction-model families, showing reduced token cost while matching or improving aggregate full-workflow accuracy in the tested settings.
watch_item: Skip decisions depend on calibration quality and guard design, so a miscalibrated safety model could reject useful skips or allow harmful ones.
paper_title: Learning What to Skip: Counterfactual Credit Assignment for Efficient Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
